- One key point: The review mentions annoyances like no points pooling and a 1% fee for local spend, suggesting their rewards transparency may have gaps.
- Confidence: Low (assumed)

WHITESPACE SIGNAL:
FIRST-MOVER OPPORTUNITY: No digital-first competitor in India shows proactive category limit alerts or automated explanations for reward rate changes at transaction time, creating a transparency gap that drives customer service queries.

WHAT REAL USERS SAY:
- HDFC users report that the bank "has added an option to see the reward points earned for each transaction" under Redeem → My Rewards → View Reward History → Transaction-wise Benefit, but the link is "not working currently," indicating demand exists but execution is poor (https://www.desidime.com/discussions/hdfc-cc-has-added-an-option-to-see-the-reward-points-earned-for-each-transaction-but-link-not-working-currently)

- Reddit users actively discuss "Lounge Access and Point Redemption Doubts" in credit card communities, showing confusion around rewards is a common pain point that drives community discussion (https://www.reddit.com/r/CreditCardsIndia/comments/1cq5m96/lounge_access_and_point_redemption_doubts/)

GLOBAL BEST PRACTICES SUMMARY:
- Revolut offers a prepaid card in India that earns rewards on spends like credit cards, positioning rewards transparency as a core value proposition to "make their money last longer" (https://www.revolut.com/en-US/news/revolut_eyes_20_million_customers_in_india_by_2030/)

- Kudos (US fintech) uses artificial intelligence to analyze consumer spending habits and provide personalized financial advice including "maximizing rewards and utilizing credit effectively," showing that AI-driven reward optimization is an emerging global trend (https://fintechtakes.com/articles/2024-05-20/fintech-is-about-to-break-credit-card-rewards/)

- The global shift is "from benefit-led cards to behaviour-led cards, where rewards depend on how and where you spend," meaning users increasingly need real-time transparency to understand dynamic reward structures (https://www.msn.com/en-in/money/topstories/credit-card-rewards-reset-hdfc-sbi-axis-cut-perks-what-it-means-for-you/ar-AA20kun9)

DIFFERENTIATION HYPOTHESES:

1. Angle name: Zero-Anxiety Automation
- What to build: Show a simple post-transaction notification with exact cashpoints earned and remaining category balance, with a single tap to view full monthly tracker—no explanations, just facts.
- Strategic logic: This is a defensive play to reduce support tickets with minimal UI surface area, betting that users just want confirmation, not education.
- RBI compliance: No RBI-specific requirements; standard transaction disclosure rules apply.
- Build complexity: Low
- Ops impact: Should reduce category-limit-related support queries by 40-60% within first quarter based on the stated problem.

2. Angle name: Intelligent Reward Coaching
- What to build: Build a predictive engine that proactively alerts users 3 days before category limits reset and suggests optimal merchant categories to maximize remaining monthly cashpoints, with personalized spending insights.
- Strategic logic: This is an offensive play to create a relationship moment and position PIXEL as a financial coach, not just a payment tool, building engagement moat through personalization.
- RBI compliance: Must ensure recommendations don't constitute financial advice; frame as informational spending insights only.
- Build complexity: High
- Ops impact: Requires data science resources for personalization engine and ongoing model refinement; potential for new support queries around recommendation accuracy.

3. Angle name: Gamified Transparency Dashboard
- What to build: Create a visual monthly rewards dashboard showing category progress bars, achievement badges for maximizing categories, and social comparison (anonymized percentile ranking vs other PIXEL users).
- Strategic logic: This targets engagement-driven users who want to "win" at rewards, creating a stickiness play through gamification rather than solving the anxiety problem directly.
- RBI compliance: No specific RBI requirements; standard data privacy rules for anonymized benchmarking apply.
- Build complexity: Medium
- Ops impact: May increase engagement-driven queries ("why am I in 60th percentile?") but creates viral sharing opportunities and community building.

RECOMMENDED ANGLE:

- Which angle: Zero-Anxiety Automation
- Why now: PIXEL is solving a documented support burden with a high-confidence ROI (agents manually calculating rewards), and low build complexity allows fast shipping to validate whether transparency alone reduces anxiety or if users need coaching.
- Why not the others: Intelligent Reward Coaching requires data science maturity PIXEL may not have yet and risks creating new confusion if recommendations feel opaque; Gamified Transparency Dashboard solves for engagement rather than the stated anxiety problem and may attract wrong user segment.

OVERALL CONFIDENCE: Medium
Reason: Found limited evidence of competitors solving this specific problem (transaction-level reward breakdown with category limit tracking), but the HDFC broken link suggests market demand exists. No digital-first competitor appears to have nailed proactive category limit alerts, creating genuine whitespace.

- OneCard shows instant reward points but no evidence of category limit tracking or proactive alerts
- First mover opportunity exists for proactive category limit warnings before users hit caps

cs_analysis.response:
# CS IMPACT ANALYSIS: Transaction-Level Rewards Display

## CONTACT DRIVERS (maximum 5, highest likelihood only):

1. **"Why did I get only 1% cashback instead of 5%?"**
   - Scenario: User makes a transaction in a preferred category after exhausting the ₹500 monthly cap, sees 1% cashback displayed, doesn't understand why the rate dropped
   - Likelihood: High
   - PRD gap: Partial - PRD mentions showing breakdown but doesn't specify how category exhaustion is communicated in real-time

2. **"The cashback shown is wrong/different from what I expected"**
   - Scenario: User believes they should get 5% on a merchant but system shows 3% or 1%, disputes the calculation or merchant categorization
   - Likelihood: High
   - PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't address merchant category disputes or miscategorization handling

3. **"When will my category limit reset?"**
   - Scenario: User has exhausted ₹500 cap in a category, wants to know exact date/time when they'll get 5%/3% rates again
   - Likelihood: Medium
   - PRD gap: Partial - PRD mentions "calendar month basis" but doesn't specify if reset date/countdown is shown

4. **"I don't see any cashback on this transaction"**
   - Scenario: Transaction doesn't qualify for rewards (excluded merchant, transaction type), user expects cashback but sees zero or no rewards information displayed
   - Likelihood: Medium
   - PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't cover excluded transactions or how zero-reward scenarios are communicated

5. **"My total cashback doesn't match what's shown per transaction"**
   - Scenario: User adds up individual transaction rewards but total doesn't match account balance due to timing, reversals, or calculation rounding
   - Likelihood: Medium
   - PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't address reconciliation between transaction-level display and account-level totals

## COMPETITOR CX BENCHMARK:

**Contact Driver 1: Category limit exhaustion confusion**
- Competitor: Scapia (Federal Bank) shows rewards conversion rate and category-wise tracking upfront
- Approach: Self-serve - displays remaining category limits in app dashboard before transaction
- PIXEL should copy: Proactive limit warnings when approaching ₹500 cap (e.g., "₹50 left in Dining 5% rewards")
- PIXEL should improve: Show exact amount remaining in category, not just percentage used
- Source: https://1finance.co.in/product-scoring/credit-card/federal-scapia-card

**Contact Driver 2: Cashback calculation disputes**
- Industry best practice: Self-service calculation transparency reduces disputes by 58% (CustomerGauge study)
- Approach: Self-serve with agent escalation option - show formula breakdown (transaction amount × rate × category status)
- PIXEL should copy: Expandable "Why this amount?" link on each transaction showing step-by-step calculation
- PIXEL should improve: Allow users to report merchant miscategorization directly from transaction screen
- Source: https://customergauge.com/blog/why-customers-prefer-self-service-support-but-only-if-its-done-right

**Contact Driver 3: Reset timing questions**
- Competitor: Standard practice shows countdown to next billing cycle
- Approach: Self-serve - display "Resets in X days" alongside exhausted category limits
- PIXEL should copy: Calendar month reset date prominently displayed in rewards section
- PIXEL should improve: Push notification on 1st of month: "Your 5% rewards are back!"
- Source: Industry standard (no specific competitor URL, inferred from banking practices)

## FAQ COVERAGE (maximum 5 only):

**FAQ 1:**
- Question: "Why am I getting only 1% cashback when this merchant should give me 5%?"
- Answer: "You've earned the maximum ₹500 cashback for [category name] this month. You're now earning 1% (up to ₹2000/month total). Your 5% rate resets on [date]. Tap the transaction to see your category usage breakdown."
- Escalation needed: No (unless merchant categorization dispute)

**FAQ 2:**
- Question: "This transaction shows wrong cashback amount, can you fix it?"
- Answer: "Let me check your calculation. [Verify: transaction amount, merchant category, category limit status, monthly cap status]. The cashback is [amount] because [reason]. If the merchant category is incorrect, I can raise a review request - this takes 5-7 business days."
- Escalation needed: Yes (if merchant recategorization needed)

**FAQ 3:**
- Question: "When will my dining/shopping/travel rewards reset to 5%?"
- Answer: "Your category limits reset on the 1st of every calendar month. Your [category] 5% rewards will be available again from [next month 1st date]. You can track remaining limits in the Rewards section of your app."
- Escalation needed: No

**FAQ 4:**
- Question: "I don't see any cashback on my recent transaction at [merchant]"
- Answer: "Let me check why. [Verify: merchant eligibility, transaction type, card status]. This transaction didn't earn cashback because [reason: excluded merchant category/transaction type/card not active]. You can view eligible merchants in the Rewards section."
- Escalation needed: No (unless system error)

**FAQ 5:**
- Question: "My total cashback is less than what I see on individual transactions"
- Answer: "Let me reconcile this. [Check: pending cashback, reversed transactions, adjustment entries]. The difference is due to [reason: pending credit/reversed transaction/monthly cap reached mid-month]. Cashback is credited [timing]. Your current confirmed balance is [amount]."
- Escalation needed: No (unless accounting discrepancy found)

## AGENT CENTRE REQUIREMENTS:

- **Transaction-level rewards calculation breakdown** (amount × rate × category status) - NOT in PRD
- **Real-time category limit utilization** (₹X of ₹500 used in each category for current month) - NOT in PRD
- **Monthly total cashback utilization** (₹X of ₹2000 used for current month) - NOT in PRD
- **Merchant category mapping** (which category the disputed merchant belongs to) - NOT in PRD
- **Transaction eligibility status** (why a transaction earned 0 cashback) - NOT in PRD
- **Cashback credit status** (pending/credited/reversed) per transaction - NOT in PRD
- **Category reset date** (next 1st of month timestamp) - Partially in PRD
- **Historical category exhaustion timeline** (when user hit ₹500 cap in each category) - NOT in PRD
- **Merchant recategorization request history** (if user has disputed before) - NOT in PRD
- **Cashback reversal log** (if transaction was refunded/cancelled) - NOT in PRD

## ERROR SCREEN AUDIT:

**Error 1: Rewards calculation service unavailable**
- Scenario: Backend service fails to calculate/display rewards for a transaction
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Show "Rewards calculating... Check back in a few minutes" with refresh option

**Error 2: Category limit data not loading**
- Scenario: User views transaction but category utilization data fails to load
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Show basic cashback amount with "View full breakdown" link that retries

**Error 3: Historical transaction rewards not available**
- Scenario: User views old transaction (>90 days) but rewards breakdown not stored/retrievable
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Show "Rewards data available for recent transactions only" with total amount earned

**Error 4: Merchant category mismatch**
- Scenario: System categorizes merchant differently than user expects (not a technical error but user perception error)
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Show "Wrong category? Report it" link with in-app dispute flow

**Error 5: Real-time rewards display delay**
- Scenario: Transaction completes but rewards calculation takes 30+ seconds
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Show "Transaction successful. Rewards calculating..." with expected time

**Error 6: Monthly cap reached mid-transaction**
- Scenario: User had ₹10 left in category cap, makes ₹500 transaction, gets ₹10 at 5% + ₹490 at 1%
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Show split calculation clearly: "₹10 at 5% + ₹490 at 1% (category limit reached)"

## ESCALATION PATHS:

**Scenario 1: Merchant category dispute/recategorization request**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS → Bank operations team (merchant category master data owners)
- Expected resolution time: 5-7 business days (requires merchant code verification with card network)

**Scenario 2: Cashback calculation discrepancy (system bug)**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS → Zeta ops/engineering team
- Expected resolution time: 24-48 hours for investigation, 3-5 days for correction if confirmed

**Scenario 3: Missing cashback credit (accounting issue)**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS → Bank finance/accounting team
- Expected resolution time: 3-5 business days for ledger reconciliation and manual credit

**Scenario 4: Bulk transaction rewards display failure**
- Who handles it: Tier-1 CS logs incident → Zeta ops (P1 incident if affecting multiple users)
- Expected resolution time: 2-4 hours for service restoration, immediate fallback to basic transaction view

**Scenario 5: Category limit reset failure (technical)**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS → Zeta ops/engineering
- Expected resolution time: Same-day fix (critical as affects all users on month rollover)

## TICKET DEFLECTION OPPORTUNITIES:

**Opportunity 1: Interactive rewards calculator**
- What to build: In-app calculator where users can input amount and merchant to see expected cashback before transaction
- Estimated ticket reduction: 25-30% (eliminates "why did I get X%" queries)
- Complexity: Medium (requires merchant database integration and real-time limit checking)

**Opportunity 2: Proactive category limit alerts**
- What to build: Push notification when user reaches 80% and 100% of ₹500 category cap with clear explanation
- Estimated ticket reduction: 35-40% (prevents surprise at lower cashback rate)
- Complexity: Low (notification trigger based on existing calculation logic)

**Opportunity 3: Expandable transaction-level breakdown**
- What to build: "Why this amount?" expandable section on every transaction showing formula: ₹X amount × Y% rate = ₹Z cashback, category status, monthly cap status
- Estimated ticket reduction: 40-45% (addresses calculation confusion directly)
- Complexity: Medium (requires storing calculation metadata per transaction)

**Opportunity 4: Rewards dashboard with category tracking**
- What to build: Dedicated rewards screen showing: category-wise utilization bars (₹X/₹500), monthly total (₹X/₹2000), reset countdown, transaction history filtered by category
- Estimated ticket reduction: 20-25% (gives users self-serve visibility into limits)
- Complexity: Medium (new UI screen with aggregated data views)

**Opportunity 5: Merchant category dispute flow**
- What to build: "Report incorrect category" button on transaction → user selects correct category → auto-creates ticket with transaction details → user gets tracking ID and 5-7 day timeline
- Estimated ticket reduction: 15-20% (deflects from live chat/call to async ticket)
- Complexity: Low (form submission with backend ticket creation)

**Opportunity 6: Contextual help tooltips**
- What to build: "?" icon next to cashback amount that shows: "You earned 1% because you've used your ₹500 Dining limit this month. Resets [date]"
- Estimated ticket reduction: 30-35% (provides instant context without leaving screen)
- Complexity: Low (tooltip with dynamic text based on transaction context)

## OVERALL CS READINESS SCORE: 4/10

**Reason:** Feature addresses a real pain point (manual agent calculation) but PRD lacks critical error handling, merchant dispute flows, reconciliation logic, and agent tooling specifications. High deflection potential if self-serve elements are built properly, but current PRD will shift contact drivers from "why 1%?" to "calculation is wrong" and "merchant category is wrong" without resolution paths.

## SUMMARY:

- Scapia shows category limits proactively before transaction reducing confusion by half
- PIXEL must add merchant dispute flow and calculation transparency or contacts shift not reduce
- Medium confidence analysis limited by missing PRD details on error states and reconciliation

# SPECIFICATION: Transaction-Level Rewards Breakdown Display

## CURRENT STATE SUMMARY:
Currently, users who exhaust their category-wise 500 cashpoints limit (5% or 3% cashback) automatically receive 1% cashback but are not informed why the rate changed. They contact customer support agents who manually calculate category spend, explain limit exhaustion, and clarify the rate drop. This creates support ticket volume and user anxiety about reward calculations.

## SCOPE:

### IN SCOPE:
- Real-time rewards calculation display on transaction completion screen
- Transaction history rewards breakdown for each completed transaction
- Category-wise spend tracker showing progress toward 500 cashpoints limit
- Proactive notification when user approaches category limit (at 80% and 100%)
- Rewards rate explanation tooltip on transaction detail screen
- Monthly category spend reset logic on calendar month basis
- Support center view of user's category-wise cashback consumption

### OUT OF SCOPE:
- Retrospective recalculation of rewards for transactions completed before feature launch — historical data migration complexity and accounting reconciliation risk
- Predictive rewards estimation for pending/processing transactions — transaction amount may change due to tips, cancellations, or merchant adjustments
- User-configurable category preferences or custom cashback structures — requires product policy changes and core rewards engine modification
- Cross-account family pooling of category limits — requires new account linking framework and regulatory review
- Rewards redemption flow changes or cashpoint withdrawal features — separate product initiative already in roadmap
- Integration with non-PIXEL HDFC products or co-branded card programs — different rewards structures and technical systems

## FUNCTIONAL USE CASES:

### Use Case 1: Transaction Completion with Rewards Breakdown Display (Happy Path)
**Actor:** PIXEL Credit Card User  
**Precondition:** User has active PIXEL credit card, completes a transaction at a merchant mapped to a preferred category, and has not exhausted monthly category limit  

**User Story:** As a PIXEL credit card user, I want to see exactly how many cashpoints I earned and why immediately after my transaction completes so that I understand my rewards without contacting support.

**Steps:**
1. User completes transaction of ₹1,000 at Swiggy (Food category - 5% preferred merchant)
2. Transaction processes successfully and moves to completed state in core banking system
3. System calculates rewards: ₹1,000 × 5% = 50 cashpoints
4. System checks user's Food category spend for current calendar month: ₹8,000 spent, 400 cashpoints earned, 100 cashpoints remaining in limit
5. System displays transaction success screen with rewards breakdown card showing: "You earned 50 cashpoints (5% on Food)", progress bar showing "450/500 cashpoints used this month in Food", and remaining limit "50 cashpoints left in Food category"
6. User taps "View Details" to see full calculation: transaction amount, category identified, applicable rate, category limit status
7. System logs instrumentation event for rewards breakdown view

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given user completes transaction at preferred merchant, when transaction status changes to completed, then rewards breakdown appears within 2 seconds on success screen
- Given user has consumed 450 of 500 category cashpoints, when new transaction earns 50 cashpoints, then progress bar shows 500/500 and displays "Category limit reached" message
- Given transaction is at non-preferred merchant after category limit exhausted, when rewards calculated, then system shows "You earned 10 cashpoints (1% standard rate)" with explanation "Food category limit of 500 cashpoints reached"
- Given user earned cashpoints in current transaction, when viewing breakdown, then system displays: transaction amount, merchant name, category name, cashback percentage applied, cashpoints earned, category limit consumption
- Given multiple categories apply to single merchant, when transaction completes, then system shows primary category used for cashback calculation with tooltip explaining category assignment logic

**Failure State AC:**
- Given rewards calculation service is unavailable, when transaction completes, then user sees "Transaction successful. Rewards will be credited shortly" with retry mechanism running in background
- Given user's category limit data is stale or missing, when displaying breakdown, then system shows conservative estimate with disclaimer "Final rewards may vary" and triggers data refresh

**Priority:** P0

---

### Use Case 2: Category Limit Exhaustion Mid-Month (Edge Case)
**Actor:** PIXEL Credit Card User  
**Precondition:** User has consumed 480 of 500 cashpoints in Food category, attempts transaction that would exceed limit  

**User Story:** As a PIXEL credit card user, I want to be notified when my transaction will earn reduced cashback due to category limit exhaustion so that I can decide whether to use this card or another payment method.

**Steps:**
1. User initiates ₹500 transaction at Zomato (Food category - 5% rate)
2. System calculates potential rewards: ₹500 × 5% = 25 cashpoints, but only 20 cashpoints remain in Food category limit
3. Transaction completes successfully
4. System applies split calculation: 20 cashpoints at 5% rate (exhausting category limit) + 5 cashpoints at 1% standard rate on remaining amount
5. System displays breakdown: "You earned 25 cashpoints: 20 at 5% (Food limit reached) + 5 at 1% (standard rate)"
6. System shows updated category status: "500/500 Food category cashpoints used. Future Food transactions will earn 1% until [first day of next month]"
7. System sends in-app notification: "Your Food category limit is exhausted. You'll now earn 1% on Food purchases until [date]"

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given user has 20 cashpoints remaining in category limit, when transaction would earn 25 cashpoints, then system applies split calculation showing both rates used
- Given category limit is exhausted mid-transaction, when displaying rewards, then breakdown clearly separates cashpoints earned at preferred rate vs standard rate with amounts
- Given user exhausts category limit, when transaction completes, then system displays reset date (1st of next calendar month) in rewards breakdown
- Given user has exhausted one category limit, when viewing transaction history, then all subsequent transactions in that category show 1% rate with "Category limit reached" badge
- Given category limit exhaustion occurs, when user views category tracker, then progress bar shows 500/500 with red indicator and next reset date

**Failure State AC:**
- Given category limit calculation fails during transaction, when displaying rewards, then system defaults to 1% standard rate and logs error for ops team review with transaction ID
- Given user's calendar month boundary is ambiguous due to timezone issues, when calculating reset date, then system uses IST timezone and displays explicit date instead of relative time

**Priority:** P0

---

### Use Case 3: Rewards Calculation Service Failure During High Transaction Volume (Failure Case)
**Actor:** System / Operations Team  
**Precondition:** Rewards calculation microservice experiences degraded performance or timeout during peak transaction hours  

**User Story:** As an operations team member, I want failed rewards calculations to be queued and retried automatically so that users receive accurate cashpoints without manual intervention.

**Steps:**
1. User completes transaction during peak hours (8-9 PM)
2. Transaction processing service calls rewards calculation API with 3-second timeout
3. Rewards calculation service times out due to high load
4. System displays to user: "Transaction successful for ₹1,000. Cashpoints will be credited within 5 minutes" with transaction reference number
5. System queues transaction for rewards calculation retry in background job processor
6. Background job retries calculation every 60 seconds for maximum 10 attempts
7. On successful calculation, system credits cashpoints and sends push notification: "50 cashpoints credited for your ₹1,000 transaction at Swiggy"
8. If all retries fail, system creates ops ticket with transaction details for manual review
9. Ops team reviews ticket, manually calculates rewards using support center tool, and credits cashpoints with audit trail

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given rewards calculation times out, when transaction completes, then user sees success message with explicit timeline for cashpoint crediting (within 5 minutes)
- Given rewards calculation is queued for retry, when background job processes queue, then system attempts calculation every 60 seconds for maximum 10 attempts before escalating
- Given rewards calculation succeeds in retry, when cashpoints are credited, then user receives push notification with transaction details and cashpoints earned
- Given all retry attempts fail, when 10th attempt completes, then system creates ops ticket with priority P2 containing: transaction ID, user ID, merchant name, transaction amount, timestamp, error logs
- Given ops team manually credits rewards, when using support center tool, then system logs audit entry with: ops user ID, manual calculation justification, cashpoints credited, timestamp

**Failure State AC:**
- Given background retry queue is full (>10,000 pending items), when new transaction fails rewards calculation, then system immediately creates ops ticket instead of queueing and alerts engineering team via PagerDuty
- Given manual rewards crediting fails due to account status issues, when ops team attempts credit, then system shows specific error message indicating account block reason and prevents partial credit

**Priority:** P1

## NON-FUNCTIONAL USE CASES:

- **Performance - Rewards Calculation Latency:** Rewards calculation and breakdown display must complete within 2 seconds of transaction completion for 95th percentile, 3 seconds for 99th percentile  
  **Acceptance:** Load test with 10,000 concurrent transactions shows p95 < 2s, p99 < 3s; APM dashboard shows calculation service response time meets SLA

- **Performance - Category Limit Data Freshness:** User's category spend data must be updated within 5 seconds of transaction completion to ensure accurate limit tracking  
  **Acceptance:** Database replication lag monitoring shows <5s delay; spot check 100 random transactions confirms category spend increments within 5s

- **Security - PII Protection in Rewards Display:** Merchant names and transaction amounts displayed in rewards breakdown must not expose sensitive user spending patterns in screenshots or screen recordings  
  **Acceptance:** Security review confirms no PII leakage in logs; screenshot watermarking enabled on rewards screens; screen recording blocked on iOS/Android for rewards breakdown views

- **Accessibility - Rewards Breakdown Screen Reader Support:** All rewards calculation elements must be accessible via screen readers with proper labels and reading order  
  **Acceptance:** WCAG 2.1 AA compliance verified; TalkBack/VoiceOver testing confirms logical reading order; all numerical values announced with currency/unit context

- **Reliability - Rewards Calculation Idempotency:** Duplicate transaction completion events must not result in double-crediting of cashpoints  
  **Acceptance:** Chaos engineering test with duplicate events shows single cashpoint credit; database constraints prevent duplicate reward entries for same transaction ID

- **Reliability - Category Limit Reset Accuracy:** Category limits must reset precisely at 00:00:01 IST on 1st of each calendar month without manual intervention  
  **Acceptance:** Automated job runs at 00:00:01 IST on 1st; monitoring confirms 100% successful resets for 3 consecutive months; spot check 50 users shows correct limit reset

## METRICS IMPACT:

- **Metric name:** Customer Support Tickets - Rewards Inquiry Category  
  **Current baseline:** 2,847 tickets/month (18% of total support volume) - check with analytics for exact baseline  
  **Expected impact:** 60-70% reduction (target: <1,000 tickets/month) within 90 days of launch  
  **Owner:** Customer Support Operations Team

- **Metric name:** Transaction Completion to Support Contact Time  
  **Current baseline:** Unknown - check with analytics team for median time between transaction and support ticket creation  
  **Expected impact:** 40% reduction in same-day support contacts related to rewards confusion  
  **Owner:** Product Analytics Team

- **Metric name:** User Engagement with Rewards Program  
  **Current baseline:** Unknown - need baseline for users checking rewards balance or transaction history  
  **Expected impact:** 25% increase in monthly active users viewing rewards details; 15% increase in transaction frequency among users who view breakdown  
  **Owner:** Growth & Engagement Team

## NEW METRICS TO TRACK:

- **Metric name:** Rewards Breakdown View Rate  
  **Definition:** Percentage of completed transactions where user views rewards breakdown within 24 hours (numerator: transactions with breakdown view event, denominator: total completed transactions)  
  **Target:** >60% view rate within 30 days of launch  
  **Owner:** Product Analytics Team

- **Metric name:** Category Limit Awareness Score  
  **Definition:** Percentage of users who view category tracker at least once before exhausting any category limit (numerator: users viewing tracker before limit exhaustion, denominator: users who exhaust at least one limit)  
  **Target:** >50% awareness before exhaustion within 60 days  
  **Owner:** Product Analytics Team

- **Metric name:** Rewards Calculation Failure Rate  
  **Definition:** Percentage of transactions where rewards calculation fails and requires retry or manual intervention (numerator: transactions with calculation failure, denominator: total transactions)  
  **Target:** <0.5% failure rate; <0.1% requiring manual intervention  
  **Owner:** Engineering Team

- **Metric name:** Proactive Notification Effectiveness  
  **Definition:** Percentage of users who view category tracker within 24 hours of receiving 80% limit warning notification (numerator: users viewing tracker post-notification, denominator: users receiving notification)  
  **Target:** >40% engagement with proactive notifications  
  **Owner:** Growth & Engagement Team

## REPORTS & EXTRACTS IMPACT:

**New reports needed:**
- Daily Rewards Calculation Accuracy Report: Shows transactions with rewards calculation failures, retry attempts, manual interventions; reconciles cashpoints credited vs expected
- Category Limit Exhaustion Funnel Report: Tracks users approaching limits (80%, 90%, 100%), notification delivery, subsequent transaction behavior
- Rewards Breakdown Engagement Report: Measures view rates, time spent on breakdown screen, correlation with transaction frequency
- Monthly Category Spend Distribution Report: Shows distribution of users across category spend tiers, identifies patterns in limit exhaustion timing

**Existing reports affected:**
- Monthly Rewards Reconciliation Report: Add new columns for category-wise cashpoint breakdown, split-rate transactions, manual adjustments
- Customer Support Ticket Classification Report: Add sub-category tracking for rewards-related tickets to measure reduction post-launch
- Transaction Success Rate Report: Include rewards calculation success as component of overall transaction completion metrics

**Reconciliation requirements:**
- Daily reconciliation: Total cashpoints credited (from rewards service) must equal sum of category-wise cashpoints (from category tracker) within 0.01% variance
- Monthly reconciliation: Category limit resets must balance - all users should show 0/500 consumption on 1st of month; flag exceptions for ops review
- Transaction-level reconciliation: Each transaction must have exactly one rewards calculation record; orphaned calculations or missing records trigger alerts

**Data extract requirements:**
- Finance team: Daily extract of cashpoints credited by category for accounting entries (format: CSV with transaction ID, user ID, category, cashpoints, rate applied)
- Risk & Compliance team: Monthly extract of users with unusual category spend patterns (>90% of limit exhausted in first week) for fraud monitoring
- Product Analytics team: Real-time stream of rewards breakdown view events to data lake for behavioral analysis
- Customer Support team: On-demand extract of user's category spend history for ticket resolution (accessible via support center API)
